deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1983-84 notes on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', i.e. arrangements of pseudolines D in a projective plane X. The page is written on the back of reused 1982 CRAY-2 printout paper. Each such arrangement gives a 'carte' (a cellular decomposition, or map) of X. X_0 is the naive map: the vertices are the intersection points and the edges are segments of the pseudolines. Some vertices and faces are 'supersingular', meaning more than two lines pass through them, or they are otherwise degenerate.

The page compares modified maps. The map X_1 was apparently obtained by blowing up the supersingular vertices into small disks or circles ('disques sommets'). The map X_2 is obtained from X_0 in two steps:
- the supersingular vertices are blown up as in X_1;
- the supersingular faces are doubled, and antipodal points on their boundary are identified. This is a cross-cap-type modification, which is natural in RP^2, where a pseudoline is one-sided.

This construction makes explicit that each pseudoline D is embedded in the space. In X_2 every face can be regarded as a polygon of type '≡ (4n)', i.e. with number of sides divisible by 4. Every vertex has even order, and in fact order 4, so all crossings become simple (two-curve, transversal) crossings.

On this map the data Rel(D), presumably the relative-position or relation data attached to the pseudolines, form a local system (a locally constant sheaf). It suffices to check this around the vertex disks, which is the 'critère de vérification'.

On the free boundaries he notes that, for D ⊂ X, they glue to faces. He then states the remaining defect: X_2 apparently does not map to X ('ne s'envoie pas dans X', sauf erreur). Point 4) begins: the map X_3 does not have this defect.

The red-circled marginal note asks why, for analogous reasons, Rel(D) should not already be a local system on X_0, then adds 'perhaps false!'. He admits he is no longer 'dans le coup' and would need to reread the notes of the preceding weeks.

So the page serves a combinatorial-topological programme: finding a canonical cell structure on the plane attached to a pseudoline arrangement, regular enough (all vertices 4-valent, faces 4n-gons) that the arrangement data become a locally constant coefficient system.
errors: No definite mathematical error can be asserted. Two points are tentative by his own account: the claim that X_2 does not map to X is qualified 'sauf erreur', and the local-system property on X_0 is left open ('peut-être faux!').
Gap: the precise definition of Rel(D) and of the maps X_1, X_3 lies on other pages. The verification criterion around the vertex disks is only asserted, not carried out here.

ideas.what: Resolving multiple points of a pseudoline arrangement by blowing vertices up into disks, so that all crossings become simple (4-valent vertices)
ideas.modern_name: Perturbation or simplification of arrangements; truncation of the arrangement cell complex; resolution of multiple points in wiring diagrams
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) and Goodman-Pollack (1980s) for perturbations to simple arrangements; standard in oriented-matroid theory (Folkman-Lawrence 1978)

ideas.what: Doubling supersingular faces and identifying antipodal boundary points (cross-cap surgery) to obtain a map whose faces are 4n-gons and whose vertices all have order 4
ideas.modern_name: Cellular surgery on maps on RP^2 / dessins-type combinatorial maps

ideas.what: Arrangement data Rel(D) forming a local system on a suitable cell decomposition, with the condition checked locally around vertex disks
ideas.modern_name: Local coefficient systems / constructible sheaves attached to arrangements; cf. sheaf-theoretic and stratified approaches to oriented matroids
ideas.where_published: Possibly related in spirit to 'cartes' and tame topology in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this construction

missed.claim: Open question whether the relative-position data Rel(D) of a pseudoline arrangement already form a local system on the naive map X_0, or only after blowing up the supersingular cells. Grothendieck suspected it might be false and left it unresolved here.
missed.quote: Mais pourquoi pour les raisons analogues, ne serait-il pas vrai qu'on a un syst. local sur X_0 (ce qui est peut-être faux!)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precise, checkable question about the sheaf-theoretic behaviour of oriented-matroid or pseudoline data on non-simple arrangements. Its interest depends on the definition of Rel(D), which is on other pages; it is likely elementary once that is known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page of an unpublished study of pseudoline arrangements, comparing several regularised cell maps. The specific face-doubling/antipodal construction and the 'local system' viewpoint are archive-only details. They are mostly technical, the key objects are defined elsewhere, and nothing here is clearly a result absent from the oriented-matroid literature.
transcription_corrections: 'en ceux de X_1' probably reads 'comme dans X_1' or 'en cercles de X_1'; uncertain.
End of the 'vérification' line: 'autrefois' should likely read 'autour', continuing on the next line as 'autour des disques sommets'.
'Cette carte est satisfaisante encore' is likely 'Cette carte a d'insatisfaisant encore', since he goes on to state a defect.
'ne s'amuse pas des X' is likely 'ne s'envoie pas dans X' (the map X_2 does not map to X); point 4) then refers to 'ce dernier inconvénient'.
Face description: 'des ≡ (4n)' suggests faces with number of sides ≡ 0 mod 4 (4n-gons); the struck-out symbol is crossed out.
Struck-out '(mais' before '– donc que sur X_0' confirmed; the 'X_0' there is overwritten or crossed.
Marginal note: 'car je ne suis plus trop dans le coup, et devrait reconsulter des notes des semaines précédentes' (read 'devrais').
